name: Loop Guard
description: Detects repeated OpenClaw tool failures and blocks unproductive retry loops.

driverModel.description: Model acting as the primary reasoning driver, for example qwen-local/qwen36-uncensored-llamacpp.

executorModel.description: Higher-capability model recommended for tool execution escalation, for example openai/gpt-5.5 or anthropic/claude-sonnet.

handoffOnAgentFailure.description: When true, start a handoff when an agent turn ends with a model/session-level failure such as stopReason=length or non_deliverable_terminal_turn.

handoffToolsAllow.description: Tool allow-list passed to the plugin-owned handoff subagent. Empty means no tools are exposed.

approvedHandoffToolsAllow.description: Default tool allow-list used when a human runs /loop-guard approve latest.

approvedHandoffWriteRoots.description: Filesystem roots the approved handoff executor may write under. Empty means no writes are approved.

approvedHandoffAllowRiskyOperations.description: When true, a human approve command is enough to authorize configured risky operation patterns for the approved handoff.

approvedHandoffMaxAgeMs.description: Maximum age of a pending handoff that /loop-guard approve may resume. Set 0 to disable age checks.

approvedHandoffRequireExecTimeout.description: Require approved executor prompts to use explicit timeouts or bounded guards for exec commands.

approvedHandoffRiskyPatterns.description: Operation patterns that require separate approval unless the approve command includes confirm=risky.

paramsPreviewMaxChars.description: Maximum length of the redacted tool-argument preview included in audit events and handoff prompts; 0 disables previews.

noProgressDetectionEnabled.description: When true, repeated successful high-risk tool calls can be treated as a no-progress loop and rewritten with guidance.

noProgressTools.description: Successful tool calls from these tools are tracked for repeated no-progress action shapes.
